items.d: One page for every attendance rule instead of seven screens.

detail.thesis: Attendance rules are spread across disconnected configuration screens, so nobody can see the full rule set that applies to an employee. The work covers: single consolidated configuration surface, rule precedence made explicit and validation across conflicting rules. It sits behind working hours, overtime, underworked, rest day and day relationship engines. It belongs to Defend because it deepens attendance and statutory ground that is hard to copy. [replace with the evidence]

items.d: Define standard working time per shift pattern.

strategy.dek: How PeoplesHR's roadmap capacity is allocated across upkeep, regulatory work and five strategic pillars, broken out by market for Sri Lanka, the Philippines and Indonesia.

northstar.said: Grow PeoplesHR annual recurring revenue from roughly $5.5M to $10M.

general:
Improve Time to Yes
  • The platform lacks a defined, tiered starter package, so first-time buyers have no low-friction way in.

Improve Time to Implement
  • Implementation time is currently a point of friction with timelines extending past 3 months, it should be closer to 1 month.

ph: Need to improve Payroll and Attendance compliance and localization.
Need to align the Attendance module to enable multi shift capability to cater to market demands in new industries (Education, Hospitality, Construction etc).
ELC is outdated, the platform needs a richer capability that meets current business needs.
Payroll does not support compensation planning.
Performance does not support the DOLE disciplinary flow.
Platform needs to upgrade the request tracker to be a true help desk.
Health and Well-being module is a growing need in PH.

general: Existing customers have little left to buy. Growth in Sri Lanka depends on account value rising, yet the four capabilities most likely to justify a price rise are each unfinished, unpackaged, or built for a single industry.

• The Attendance revamp is scoped to the industries we already serve rather than the ones we want to enter
  • PIT Allocation solves rostering for casinos and cannot be sold outside that vertical
  • No agent based capability exists in a form that can be sold separately
  • Recruitment has drifted from what the market is currently asking for

Delight.note: Distinct from Defend. Delight is customers who want to stay and shows up in NRR. Defend is customers who cannot leave and shows up in GRR.

general: Customer experience. Triaged modules, workflows and screens where a human remains in the loop after agentic workflows land.

Defend.note: Ordered so it stops buying the wrong moat. Depth that customers choose, not depth that traps them.

general:
External systems
  • Integrations are built per customer, not offered by the platform. Each one is paid for once rather than holding the account, and a competitor rebuilds the set in a single implementation.

Statutory depth in Payroll and Attendance
  • Statutory rules live in per-customer configuration, not in the platform. Every change is rebuilt account by account, so no customer is safer for being on PeoplesHR.

Platform usage monitoring
  • No account is tagged by which modules it uses or how deeply. We invest on anecdote, and cannot say which customers are genuinely hard to move.

Moonshots.note: High risk and high reward bets. Small enough that a failure costs a rounding error, deliberate enough that a success is not an accident.
